submission.bindingBasis: The planning-time expected state (sourceStateDigest e5d8008d..., head 4e6ce637...) does not match the current observed state (sourceStateDigest 9b29fb71..., head 050b3ffa...). The planning binding attempt already failed with REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed. There is concurrent committed work (.hp4-probe/material.txt) not present at planning time.
submission.rationale: The planning evidence reviewed a clean workspace state (digest e5d8008d) but the current boundary evidence shows a different state (digest 9b29fb71) with new committed concurrent work (.hp4-probe/material.txt). The owner contract allows workspace.close to either omit expectedSourceStateDigest or compare-and-close on an exact digest; a mismatched digest fails not_committed, which is exactly what the planningBindingAttempt shows (REVISION_MISMATCH/not_committed). Since the workspace has been changed since planning, I cannot safely close it without first reobserving the current state and re-planning the consequence. Acting against the stale planning binding would either fail (if we bind to the old digest) or risk closing a workspace with unknown concurrent work (if we act unbound). Holding also is not ideal but reobservation is the correct step to refresh the reviewed state before deciding whether to close.
